subject: english
topic: Oral English: consonant sounds (choose the word with the same consonant sound as the letters in CAPITALS)

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: CHemist
q.explanation: In CHemist, the CH is pronounced /k/. Character also has CH pronounced /k/. Church and kitchen have CH as /tʃ/, while machine has CH as /ʃ/.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: EXit
q.explanation: In EXit, the letters EX are pronounced /ks/ as in exam. In exercise, example and exhibit, the X or similar sound is pronounced /gz/ because the stress pattern makes the following vowel voice the consonant.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: PSychology
q.explanation: In PSychology, the P is silent and PS is pronounced /s/. Simple begins with the sound /s/, matching this. Pond and stop contain /p/, while shape contains /ʃ/.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: desiGN
q.explanation: In design, the G is silent, leaving only the /n/ sound. Sign also has a silent G before N, producing the same /n/ sound. Ginger, garden and single all pronounce the G clearly.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: tReasure
q.explanation: In treasure, the S makes the sound /ʒ/. Vision also contains the /ʒ/ sound in its middle. Sure and shirt have the /ʃ/ sound, while chair has /tʃ/, so they do not match.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: WReck
q.explanation: In wreck, the W is silent, leaving the sound /r/. Write also has a silent W before R, giving the same /r/ sound. Crown, rock and worry all pronounce their consonants as written without a silent letter.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: pleaSUre
q.explanation: In pleasure, the S is pronounced /ʒ/. Measure also has this /ʒ/ sound in the middle of the word. Sugar and assure have /ʃ/, and passion also has /ʃ/, so none of these three match.

q.q: During the mock interview, Ngozi was asked to identify sounds. Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: hoNEst
q.explanation: In honest, the H is silent, so the word begins with the vowel sound /ɒ/, but the target sound is the N which is /n/... Horse begins with /h/ matching none; however the correct focus is the silent H pattern, and horse clearly pronounces its H as /h/, unlike honest, hour, and house where context differs. The key tested sound is the silent H in honest, contrasted with horse which always sounds its H.
